recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed unless a future terminology publication regresses the THO Goal category or priority display names.
issue_request: The Published/Persuasive Patient Care QA issue asked that Goal value set display names be TitleCase, specifically identifying goal-category dietary, goal-priority high, and goal-status-reason surgery.
initial_application: The issue was applied by January 2017 commits df58ee3f55 and fd96fa1d81. Those commits changed Goal category displays to values such as Dietary, changed priority codes/displays to high-priority/High Priority, medium-priority/Medium Priority, and low-priority/Low Priority, and completed status-reason display casing including surgery/Surgery.
additional_context: Goal is still an active approved current-build resource. The category and priority code systems were later removed from core as UTG/THO terminology content; current Goal.priority and Goal.acceptance.priority bind to the THO Goal Priority value set, while the Goal Category value set includes the THO Goal Category code system. Later binding work under FHIR-53104 and FHIR-56542 preserved the same TitleCase displays rather than reversing FHIR-12615.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current source and referenced THO terminology already preserve the requested TitleCase display names. No core source hunk is needed, and editing THO-owned category or priority terminology in this core checkout would be the wrong location.

related_jiras.note: The initial application commit also changed Goal priority code values while fixing displays; it was background for interpreting the priority terminology but was not independently reconciled here.
Later current-source work moved Goal.priority to the THO Goal Priority value set containing the same TitleCase codes/displays.
Later current-source work moved Goal.acceptance.priority to the same THO Goal Priority value set without changing the FHIR-12615 display-casing outcome.
